extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institutions' administrators and Title IX personnel (Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, legal counsel)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for postsecondary institutions to structure and conduct Title IX sex-based harassment grievance procedures, including rules on questioning, weighing evidence, live hearings, and training. Focuses on what questions/evidence are permissible, decisionmaker duties, and options for live hearings vs. live-questioning processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of questions about sexual interests and prior sexual conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about the complainant's sexual interests are always excluded as impermissible; questions about the complainant's prior sexual conduct are excluded as impermissible unless offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct or as evidence about specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent that is offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.45(b)(7)(iii). Institutions must treat such questions as per se impermissible except for the narrow exceptions above; this is an absolute ban for sexual-interest questions and a conditional ban for prior sexual conduct questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fact-specific determination whether other prior sexual-conduct questions are harassing
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether other questions about a party's prior sexual conduct are harassing is a fact-specific determination that depends on the content of the question, the manner in which it is asked, and the purpose for which it is offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must evaluate content, tone/manner, and offered purpose when determining if a question is harassing; context can make otherwise similar questions permissible or impermissible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ban on unclear or harassing questions applies to parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: The prohibition on unclear or harassing questions applies equally to questions asked of parties and to questions asked of witnesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: §106.46(f)(3) revised to state that a postsecondary institution must not permit questions that are unclear or harassing of the party or witness being questioned. The Department intended to cover advisors questioning both parties and witnesses, not just parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions may adopt and apply other reasonable rules regarding decorum
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may 'adopt and apply other reasonable rules regarding decorum' governing questioning and conduct during grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Language revised from 'impose' to 'adopt and apply' to clarify institutions' authority; rules of decorum must be reasonable and may be used to manage hearings and questioning practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must explain exclusions and allow clarification/revision of questions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker must explain any decision to exclude a proposed question as impermissible, as well as for relevance, and must provide a party the opportunity to clarify or revise a question that the decisionmaker has determined is unclear or harassing and have the question asked if it is sufficiently clarified or revised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change to §106.46(f)(3). Requirement increases transparency and gives parties an opportunity to cure unclear/harassing formulations before exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker discretion to weigh statements by those who refuse to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker may determine, based on the totality of the circumstances, the weight to be given, if any, to a statement made by a party or witness who refuses to respond to questions deemed relevant and not impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final §106.46(f)(4) removed rigid language about 'questions related to credibility' and instead gives flexibility to consider number of questions refused, reasons for refusal (intentional evasion vs. inability to recall), whether refusal was to avoid testing earlier statements, and other contextual factors. Decisionmaker is not required to exclude such statements and may give full weight when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on drawing inferences solely from refusal to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are restricted from drawing inferences about whether sex-based harassment occurred based solely on a party's or witness's refusal to respond to questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department declined to change 'whether sex-based harassment occurred' phrasing. While a decisionmaker may consider refusal among other evidence, an adverse inference may not be based solely on refusal; this aligns with §106.46(h) and §106.45(h)(1) requiring evaluation of all relevant, non-impermissible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: §106.46(f)(4) applies to witnesses as well as parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions permitting decisionmakers to determine the weight to assign to statements by persons who refuse to respond to questions apply equally to witnesses and parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department revised §106.46(f)(4) to explicitly include witnesses, responding to commenters who requested parity between parties and witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Statements' excludes non-declarative evidence (e.g., videos)
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'statements' applies to any statement of a party or witness in its ordinary meaning, but does not include evidence (such as videos) that do not constitute a person's intent to make factual assertions, or to the extent such evidence does not contain a person's statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to 85 FR 30349. Decisionmakers should not treat non-declarative materials as 'statements' for purposes of weighing refusals to answer questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker must evaluate relevant, non-impermissible evidence for persuasiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: The decisionmaker is required to evaluate all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence for its persuasiveness when making a determination about whether sex-based harassment occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.45(h)(1). The weighting of statements by those who refused to answer must occur within this broader evidence-persuasiveness framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmakers may consider reasons and context for refusal to answer
rubrics_metrics.description: As part of weighing evidence, a decisionmaker may take into account the reasons why a party or witness refused to answer questions (e.g., intentional refusal to avoid testing earlier statements versus inability to recall) and whether they answered most questions but plausibly declined a small number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided: intentional refusal to avoid testing earlier statements suggests potential manipulation; reasonable justification for not responding to a small number of questions mitigates adverse weight. Decisionmaker uses totality of circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearings are optional; institutions must provide a live-questioning process
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations remove a universal live hearing requirement but require that a postsecondary institution provide another live-questioning process if it chooses not to use a live hearing; the chosen process must enable the decisionmaker to assess credibility to the extent credibility is in dispute and relevant to evaluating allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Department maintains that case law does not require live hearings in all cases so long as another live-questioning process exists. §106.46(g) governs live hearings; §106.46(f) governs live-questioning process alternatives. Decisionmakers can assess credibility via investigator questioning with decisionmaker review, or other live-questioning mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Live hearing may be conducted with parties physically separate or virtually
rubrics_metrics.description: If a postsecondary institution elects to use a live hearing, it may conduct the hearing with the parties physically present in separate locations, including virtually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits protections for parties who find in-person interaction traumatic and allows technological separation while still holding a live hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide each party an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an accurate description of such evidence, and a reasonable opportunity to respond; if a description is provided, parties must be given access to the evidence upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.45(f)(4). For postsecondary student-party complaints, §106.46(e)(6)(i) requires either access to the evidence or the same written investigative report that accurately summarizes evidence, with access to the underlying evidence upon request. This promotes transparency regardless of whether a live hearing is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and impartiality requirements for personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators, decisionmakers, and other persons responsible for implementing the recipient's grievance procedures must receive training on the recipient's grievance procedures, how to serve impartially (including avoiding prejudgment, conflicts of interest, and bias), the meaning and application of 'relevant' in relation to questions and evidence, and types of evidence that are impermissible regardless of relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.8(d) and §106.45(b)(2). Training is required regardless of whether live hearings are used; recipients must prohibit conflicts of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or individually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedures must be nondiscriminatory and equitable
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must carry out its grievance procedures in a nondiscriminatory manner and must treat complainants and respondents equitably (prohibition on discrimination based on sex).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.31(a)(1),(b)(4) and §106.45(b)(1). OCR may investigate complaints alleging sex discrimination in the conduct of grievance procedures; permitting optional live hearings is not considered sex discrimination per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker/investigator roles in live-questioning process
rubrics_metrics.description: In a live-questioning process where a live hearing is not used, either the investigator or the decisionmaker may ask questions of parties and witnesses during individual meetings; if the investigator asks the questions, the decisionmaker will rely on the investigator's assessment of credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites §106.46(f)(1)(i). Institutions choosing non-live-hearing approaches must ensure the inquiry and credibility assessment mechanism gives the decisionmaker sufficient ability to evaluate disputed credibility when relevant.
